bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical disruption to exports (Middle East/Europe); commodity volatility (aluminum); integration delays in Antolin synergies; execution risk in capex ramp-up; regulatory delays in EV adoption
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, aggressive, and execution-focused; strong emphasis on technology leadership, ESG credibility, and disciplined M&A; transparent on margin roadmaps but cautious on disclosure due to competition
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Antolin’s headliner dominance (75% market share) is not a ceiling — continuous model changes drive new variants, ensuring organic growth; 60% powertrain-agnostic mix is a strategic outcome of legacy business resilience, not just EV exposure; ESG certifications (CDP B, Dun & Bradstreet 2/5, EcoVadis Bronze) are material differentiators for OEM selection
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "In FY26, for the Antolin acquisition, the Company issued Non-Convertible Debentures worth Rs. 10,000 Million, which has increased the Debt" — standalone Debt-to-Equity rose to 0.59x in FY26 from 0.15x in FY25 (consolidated 0.62x from 0.19x), which the deck says "would get normalised with the repayment of the debentures".
- Elevated finance costs of Rs 252 Million (consolidated) and Rs 229 Million (standalone) in Q1FY27 to fund the Antolin acquisition are described as "a temporary effect which shall be normalised once the debt is repaid".
- Total Equity Dividend Paid (Rs Million): 134 (FY21), 220 (FY22), 330 (FY23), 440 (FY24), 440 (FY25), 440 (FY26) — flat at Rs 440 Million for three years.
- Return ratios have stepped down with the acquisition-funded balance sheet: standalone ROE 17.8% and ROCE 18.5% in FY26 versus 20.7% and 27.0% in FY25; consolidated ROE 18.6% and ROCE 18.6% in FY26 versus 20.6% and 25.5% in FY25.
- History of five bonus issues (1991, 1994, 1997, 2000 and a 1:1 on 13 Jun 2023 taking shares from 2,20,24,912 to 4,40,49,824); shareholding as on 30 June 2026 shows Promoters 43.8%, DII 12.2%, FII 8.2%, Bodies Corporate (incl. overseas) 2.0%, Others 33.9%.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- India's largest manufacturer of pistons, rings and engine valves; No.1 in piston rings in India
- Long-standing technology partnerships with Riken/NPR-Riken and Kolbenschmidt (rings), Fuji Oozx (engine valves) and Honda Foundry (pistons) of Japan/Germany
- Recognized in-house R&D centre (DISR) and strong technological capabilities across multiple powertrain solutions
- Established OEM customer base broadened via the Grupo Antolin acquisition, with a Technology Licensing Agreement providing continued access to interior/lighting know-how
- Diversified across automotive, off-highway, farm, genset, exports, aftermarket and non-automotive applications, increasing content per vehicle as a multi-domain supplier
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Global macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty — Management flags a challenging, evolving global environment marked by geopolitical uncertainties and supply chain disruptions that pressure demand, inputs and exports; exports grew only 2.36% amid this backdrop.
- Supply chain disruption and cost pressures — The Company continues to navigate external challenges including cost pressures and supply chain uncertainties, mitigated through vendor partnerships, working-capital optimisation and automation.
- Powertrain / technology transition — Shift toward electric, hybrid and alternative fuels (ethanol, biofuels, CBG, hydrogen ICE, CNG/LNG) requires continuous product development to keep the ICE-heavy core portfolio relevant and future-ready.
- Acquisition integration risk — FY2025-26 saw strategic acquisitions (auto interiors, plastic doors/trims, interior lighting); realising synergies and integrating new businesses into the multi-domain model is an execution watch-item.
- Sustainability / ESG-related risk — The Risk Management Committee explicitly identifies sustainability (particularly ESG-related) risks as part of the enterprise risk framework, alongside financial, operational, sectoral, information and cyber-security risks.
- Information and cyber-security risk — Cyber-security and information risks are named among internal/external risks the Risk Management Committee must identify, mitigate and monitor.
- Export / customer concentration and diversification dependence — Growth relies on diversifying revenue across exports, aftermarket and non-automotive applications (railways, snowmobiles, compressors, marine, defence, industrial engines); demand in any single geography or segment remains a sectoral exposure.

business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- "Leading manufacturer of pistons, piston pins, piston rings & engine valves" with more than 5 decades of industry presence; described as "#1 Exporter of Pistons, Piston Rings, Pistons Pins & Engine Valves" and present in 30+ countries across 5 continents.
- Long-standing technology partnerships with global majors — Kolbenschmidt (Germany, pistons), Riken Corporation (Japan, rings), Honda Foundry (Japan, pistons), Fuji Oozx (Japan, engine valves), Takahata (Japan, high-precision injection moulded components) and, since 2026, Antolin (Spain, automotive interior solutions).
- Part of the Shriram Group heritage founded by Dr. Charat Ram; strong credit profile with rating "upgraded to AA+ from India Ratings"; standalone Total Income and PAT stated to have grown at 15% and 33% CAGR from FY22-26.
- The deck devotes a full slide to arguing ICE demand persists — citing EV affordability (initial cost 2x an ICE vehicle), battery replacement cost up to Rs 7 lakh, 200+ EVs per commercial charging point in India versus ~20 in the US and under 10 in China, and grid constraints against India's ~540 GW installed capacity in 2026.
- Diversified revenue streams across OEM, Exports and Aftermarket, and across Automotive and Non-Automotive (tractors & off-highway, industrials, gensets, railways & defence, marine, snowmobile and lawnmower applications).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Rename] The company has been renamed SPR Auto Technologies Limited (formerly Shriram Pistons & Rings Limited); the NSE ticker remains SHRIPISTON and BSE scrip code 544344.
- [Acquisition — Antolin] SPR Auto Technologies acquired 100% stakes in SPR Auto Interior Lighting Solutions Pvt. Ltd. (formerly Antolin Lighting India), SPR Auto Interior Solutions Pvt. Ltd. (formerly Grupo Antolin India) and SPR Auto Interior Solutions Chakan Pvt. Ltd. (formerly Grupo Antolin Chakan), all completed on 08 January 2026, bringing 5 manufacturing facilities (2 each in Chakan and Pune, 1 in Chennai) and a long-term technology licensing agreement with Antolin Global.
- [Acquisitions — earlier] SEL acquired 62% of SPR Takahata Precision India (completed 16 October 2023) and 100% of SPR TGPEL Precision Engineering (completed 24 December 2024); SEL's stake in SPR EMF Innovations rose from 66.42% to 72.58% during Q2FY26 (original acquisition completed 11 January 2023); SPR Auto Technologies acquired 100% of Karna Intertech (completed 01 April 2025) as backward integration into gravity die casting moulds.
- [Exceptional item] FY26 carried an exceptional item of Rs 271 Million consolidated / Rs 237 Million standalone, described as a "Non-recurring expense pertaining to statutory impact of New Labour Code".
- [Industry sizing] Global ICE market USD 283.1 Bn (2025E) to USD 384.3 Bn (2030P) at 6.3% CAGR (source: Mordor Intelligence); Indian ICE market USD 5.4 Bn to USD 8.3 Bn at 7.6% CAGR (source: Mobility Foresights); India Auto Interior Solutions market Rs 53.4 Bn (FY26) to Rs 81.0-85.0 Bn (FY31P) at 8.7%-9.7% CAGR.
- [Partner shareholding] The technology-partnership slide carries the line "21.3% Holding in SPR Auto Technologies" positioned adjacent to the Riken Corporation entry; the extraction does not make the attribution unambiguous, and it cannot be reconciled against the 30 June 2026 shareholding buckets shown elsewhere in the deck.

outlook.body:
- Rebranded from Shriram Pistons and Rings Limited to SPR Auto Technologies Limited, with shareholder-approved alteration of the object clause and adoption of a new Memorandum of Association, signalling a broadening of scope beyond pistons and rings toward wider auto technologies
- The Board follows a formal Dividend Distribution Policy (Regulation 43A of SEBI Listing Regulations) and maintains a consistent approach to dividend pay-out, taking guidance from the policy parameters; dividends are paid out of the year's profits. For FY2025-26 an interim dividend was paid (Feb 2026) and a final dividend of Rs. 5/- per equity share was recommended, subject to AGM approval, with the balance transferred to General Reserve. The Company reports a strengthened credit profile, with India Ratings and Research (Ind-Ra) upgrading/affirming ratings at IND AA+/Stable for its credit facilities including CPs and NCDs, reflecting prudent financial management and governance.
- Renewable energy accounts for 21% of total energy; Company continues to reduce dependence on conventional energy and increase renewable share
- 100% of used water is recycled
- Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions reduced by 20%
- 95% of onboarded critical suppliers are environmentally compliant
- Deployed an ESG data tool (implemented with KPMG) for real-time tracking of ESG data and stronger disclosure credibility
- Certified to ISO 14001 (environmental management) and ISO 45001 (occupational health and safety); external assessments/disclosures include CDP, EcoVadis and SAQ
- Developing and supplying lower-carbon, future-ready products: components for CNG, LNG/PNG, ethanol-blended fuels, hydrogen-based ICE, hydrogen-enriched CNG, hybrid and electric mobility
- BRSR aligned to nine principles of the National Guidelines on Responsible Business Conduct; focus areas include GHG reduction, water conservation, circular economy, occupational health & safety, human rights and supply-chain responsibility
- Zero tolerance POSH policy with Internal Complaints Committee (nil complaints in FY2025-26); compliance with Maternity Benefit Act, 1961
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: FY2025-26 was described as a landmark year marked by robust growth, strategic acquisitions and diversification into new product categories. The Company continued to invest in expansion of manufacturing capacities and technologies to improve operational efficiency and delivery performance, and commissioned a new assembly centre supporting improved execution capabilities and readiness to meet customer requirements. The key strategic development was the acquisition, on January 8, 2026, of a 100% equity stake in three Indian entities of Spain's Grupo Antolin at an aggregate Enterprise Value of Euro 159 Million (approximately Rs. 16,700 Million) — Antolin Lighting India Private Limited (ALIPL, 100%), Grupo Antolin India Private Limited (GAIPL, 100%) and Grupo Antolin Chakan Private Limited (GACPL, ~99.99% indirect via GAIPL) — expanding its footprint into automotive interior and lighting product segments (headliner substrates, modular headliners, sunvisors, door panels, centre floor consoles, pillar trims, front-end carriers, overhead consoles, cockpit dashboards, dome lamps, ambient lighting, touch panels and capacitive pads). A Technology Licensing Agreement was entered into with Grupo Antolin, Spain, for continued access to technical know-how. The Company progressed products across multiple powertrain solutions and future technologies including electric, hybrid and alternative fuels (ethanol, biofuels and Compressed Bio Gas), and continued to diversify revenue through exports, aftermarket and non-automotive applications (railways, snowmobiles, compressors, marine, defence and industrial engines). Effective April 2, 2026 the Company was renamed from Shriram Pistons & Rings Limited to SPR Auto Technologies Limited to reflect its evolution into a multi-product, multi-domain auto components supplier. Entering FY2026-27, management stated it remains focused on strengthening operational capabilities, expanding its product portfolio and delivering long-term value while navigating geopolitical developments, cost pressures and supply chain uncertainties.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

deepdive.thesis: SPR Auto Technologies delivered record FY26 revenue (INR4,571cr, +25% YoY) and EBITDA (INR989cr, +18% YoY) driven by strategic acquisitions (Antolin, Karna) and capacity expansions, with 60% of business now powertrain-agnostic — this structural shift reduces ICE dependency and positions the company as a diversified mobility tech platform with margin expansion potential across subsidiaries.

currentContext.expansion: FY2025-26 was described as a landmark year marked by robust growth, strategic acquisitions and diversification into new product categories. The Company continued to invest in expansion of manufacturing capacities and technologies to improve operational efficiency and delivery performance, and commissioned a new assembly centre supporting improved execution capabilities and readiness to meet customer requirements. The key strategic development was the acquisition, on January 8, 2026, of a 100% equity stake in three Indian entities of Spain's Grupo Antolin at an aggregate Enterprise Value of Euro 159 Million (approximately Rs. 16,700 Million) — Antolin Lighting India Private Limited (ALIPL, 100%), Grupo Antolin India Private Limited (GAIPL, 100%) and Grupo Antolin Chakan Private Limited (GACPL, ~99.99% indirect via GAIPL) — expanding its footprint into automotive interior and lighting product segments (headliner substrates, modular headliners, sunvisors, door panels, centre floor consoles, pillar trims, front-end carriers, overhead consoles, cockpit dashboards, dome lamps, ambient lighting, touch panels and capacitive pads). A Technology Licensing Agreement was entered into with Grupo Antolin, Spain, for continued access to technical know-how. The Company progressed products across multiple powertrain solutions and future technologies including electric, hybrid and alternative fuels (ethanol, biofuels and Compressed Bio Gas), and continued to diversify revenue through exports, aftermarket and non-automotive applications (railways, snowmobiles, compressors, marine, defence and industrial engines). Effective April 2, 2026 the Company was renamed from Shriram Pistons & Rings Limited to SPR Auto Technologies Limited to reflect its evolution into a multi-product, multi-domain auto components supplier. Entering FY2026-27, management stated it remains focused on strengthening operational capabilities, expanding its product portfolio and delivering long-term value while navigating geopolitical developments, cost pressures and supply chain uncertainties.

risks.note: Management flags a challenging, evolving global environment marked by geopolitical uncertainties and supply chain disruptions that pressure demand, inputs and exports; exports grew only 2.36% amid this backdrop.

risks.risk: Supply chain disruption and cost pressures
risks.note: The Company continues to navigate external challenges including cost pressures and supply chain uncertainties, mitigated through vendor partnerships, working-capital optimisation and automation.

Shift toward electric, hybrid and alternative fuels (ethanol, biofuels, CBG, hydrogen ICE, CNG/LNG) requires continuous product development to keep the ICE-heavy core portfolio relevant and future-ready.

FY2025-26 saw strategic acquisitions (auto interiors, plastic doors/trims, interior lighting); realising synergies and integrating new businesses into the multi-domain model is an execution watch-item.

The Risk Management Committee explicitly identifies sustainability (particularly ESG-related) risks as part of the enterprise risk framework, alongside financial, operational, sectoral, information and cyber-security risks.
Cyber-security and information risks are named among internal/external risks the Risk Management Committee must identify, mitigate and monitor.

risks.risk: Export / customer concentration and diversification dependence
risks.note: Growth relies on diversifying revenue across exports, aftermarket and non-automotive applications (railways, snowmobiles, compressors, marine, defence, industrial engines); demand in any single geography or segment remains a sectoral exposure.

one-line thesis: SPR Auto Technologies delivered record FY26 revenue (INR4,571cr, +25% YoY) and EBITDA (INR989cr, +18% YoY) driven by strategic acquisitions (Antolin, Karna) and capacity expansions, with 60% of business now powertrain-agnostic — this structural shift reduces ICE dependency and positions the company as a diversified mobility tech platform with margin expansion potential across subsidiaries.
financial scorecard: revenue: +25% YoY (INR4,571cr); EBITDA/margin: +18% YoY (INR989cr, ~21.6%); PAT (rptd): +15% YoY; PAT (normalized): +17% YoY (ex-one-off acquisition integration costs); order book: Not disclosed; net debt: ~INR750cr (post NCDs for Antolin acquisition, debt-equity ~0.25x)
guidance: revenue growth: 'Healthy pipeline' with multi-year programs (2029-30); margin: Subsidiaries to approach stand-alone margin (~21-22%) within <3 years; order inflow: 'Exciting' new programs across interiors, plastics, EV motors; capex/commissioning: ~INR200cr/year over next 2-3 years; Neemrana (Takahata Phase 3), Noida (TGPEL), Pithampur (SPL Phase 3) under expansion
segment / subsidiary detail: Legacy (Pistons/Rings): 65% of revenue, +10-11% YoY growth across PVs, CVs, 2W, tractors; Antolin (Interiors/Lighting): Acquired Jan 2026, contributing to revenue, margins improving from ~9-10% to target ~20%; Takahata/TGPEL (Precision Molding): TAM ~INR3,500cr, targeting 20-30% share; EV Motors & Controllers: EBITDA positive, Coimbatore plant operational, serving 2W/4W EVs with hairpin winding tech
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion into non-automotive (medical/industrial) precision parts; export recovery in LATAM/Middle East; inorganic growth via M&A in tech-enabled auto components (e.g., sensors, ADAS, high-voltage systems); synergy-driven cross-selling between Antolin and plastics divisions
margins & cost dynamics: Commodity (aluminum +40% YoY) fully pass-through to OEMs with 1-quarter lag; labor shortages mitigated by premium wages; energy stable; margin uplift expected via in-sourcing, supply chain optimization, and synergy realization across subsidiaries

risks & watch-items: Geopolitical disruption to exports (Middle East/Europe); commodity volatility (aluminum); integration delays in Antolin synergies; execution risk in capex ramp-up; regulatory delays in EV adoption
management quality / tone: Confident, aggressive, and execution-focused; strong emphasis on technology leadership, ESG credibility, and disciplined M&A; transparent on margin roadmaps but cautious on disclosure due to competition
non-obvious takeaways: Antolin’s headliner dominance (75% market share) is not a ceiling — continuous model changes drive new variants, ensuring organic growth; 60% powertrain-agnostic mix is a strategic outcome of legacy business resilience, not just EV exposure; ESG certifications (CDP B, Dun & Bradstreet 2/5, EcoVadis Bronze) are material differentiators for OEM selection

one_liner.body: India's largest manufacturer of pistons, rings and engine valves, now repositioning as a multi-product, multi-domain auto components supplier under the SPR Auto Technologies name.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: SPR Auto Technologies Limited (formerly Shriram Pistons & Rings Limited) manufactures pistons, piston rings and engine valves for automotive, off-highway vehicles, farm equipment, genset engines and compressors. Following the FY2025-26 acquisition of Grupo Antolin's Indian operations, it has expanded beyond its core powertrain components into automotive interior solutions and interior lighting. The company supplies OEMs, aftermarket and non-automotive applications in India and export markets.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Rename] The company has been renamed SPR Auto Technologies Limited (formerly Shriram Pistons & Rings Limited); the NSE ticker remains SHRIPISTON and BSE scrip code 544344.
- [Acquisition — Antolin] SPR Auto Technologies acquired 100% stakes in SPR Auto Interior Lighting Solutions Pvt. Ltd. (formerly Antolin Lighting India), SPR Auto Interior Solutions Pvt. Ltd. (formerly Grupo Antolin India) and SPR Auto Interior Solutions Chakan Pvt. Ltd. (formerly Grupo Antolin Chakan), all completed on 08 January 2026, bringing 5 manufacturing facilities (2 each in Chakan and Pune, 1 in Chennai) and a long-term technology licensing agreement with Antolin Global.
- [Acquisitions — earlier] SEL acquired 62% of SPR Takahata Precision India (completed 16 October 2023) and 100% of SPR TGPEL Precision Engineering (completed 24 December 2024); SEL's stake in SPR EMF Innovations rose from 66.42% to 72.58% during Q2FY26 (original acquisition completed 11 January 2023); SPR Auto Technologies acquired 100% of Karna Intertech (completed 01 April 2025) as backward integration into gravity die casting moulds.
- [Exceptional item] FY26 carried an exceptional item of Rs 271 Million consolidated / Rs 237 Million standalone, described as a "Non-recurring expense pertaining to statutory impact of New Labour Code".
- [Industry sizing] Global ICE market USD 283.1 Bn (2025E) to USD 384.3 Bn (2030P) at 6.3% CAGR (source: Mordor Intelligence); Indian ICE market USD 5.4 Bn to USD 8.3 Bn at 7.6% CAGR (source: Mobility Foresights); India Auto Interior Solutions market Rs 53.4 Bn (FY26) to Rs 81.0-85.0 Bn (FY31P) at 8.7%-9.7% CAGR.
- [Partner shareholding] The technology-partnership slide carries the line "21.3% Holding in SPR Auto Technologies" positioned adjacent to the Riken Corporation entry; the extraction does not make the attribution unambiguous, and it cannot be reconciled against the 30 June 2026 shareholding buckets shown elsewhere in the deck.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.
